clue.text: Part with charge for cash dispenser in mood: it's sky high

indicators.note: for here means one thing stands in place of another, swapping a piece of the mood word

parts.note: the atmosphere of a place is its mood or feel
an ATM is an automated teller machine, a cash dispenser
an ion is an atom or particle carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about swapping a charged part into a cash machine, ending in something lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals a swap; 'Part with charge' sounds like paying a fee, but it is the physics particle.
explanation.definitionFit: This layer of the upper atmosphere lies many kilometres above the earth, high in the sky.

clue.text: Cape with crashing wave

indicators.note: crashing suggests the letters of the two words smash and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Breakers crash against a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges the eight letters of CAPE and WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitecap is a wave whose crest breaks into white foam.

clue.text: Type of language grouping

definitions.meaning: a sloping style of printed lettering
the branch of Indo-European including Latin and its relatives

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slanted typeface and the ancient language family of Italy that contains Latin.

clue.text: Rise up to father a child

indicators.note: up, as in stirred up or in disorder, tells you to rearrange the word Rise

explanation.surface: Getting up in order to become a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a reversal for a down clue, but RISE reversed is ESIR; it is an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to beget offspring, used especially of a male parent animal.

clue.text: Hard bit apt to be abhorrent

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
bit is the past tense of bite, as is ate in the sense of chewed
apt in the sense of capable or fit means able

explanation.surface: A tough piece is liable to be detestable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abhorrent deserves loathing, which is just what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Light and delicate breeze in meadow rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the assembled letters read from bottom to top
in places the breeze word inside the meadow word

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a breeze is moving air

explanation.surface: A gentle wind wafts upward across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The breeze goes inside the meadow to make LAIREA, which 'rising' turns upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy and ethereal, light as air, is the adjectival sense of this word.

clue.text: Passage of football: a mediocre game

indicators.note: Passage of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dull stretch of a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is not a sport here but the adjective meaning injured, as in a game leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A game leg is a crippled or injured one, so game is a synonym for limping.

clue.text: American writer expressing anger

indicators.note: expressing here means voicing a word, so we want something said that matches

parts.note: wroth is an old word meaning angry, full of wrath

explanation.surface: A US author venting fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Roth was an American novelist; WROTH, meaning angry, is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Roth was a celebrated US novelist, author of Portnoy's Complaint.

clue.text: As is delta wing after being nicked by pilot

indicators.note: being nicked by means the time word is taken into the test word

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a trial run
after in time means later

explanation.surface: A delta-wing aircraft, after a pilot has stolen it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like an aviator, fitting the delta wing, but here it is a test run.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta wing is triangular, having three sides.

clue.text: Road traffic accident stops return of most of cargo of vital fluid container

indicators.note: stops as in plugs: the accident letters fill the middle of the other piece
return of means the shortened cargo word runs backwards
most of means the last letter of the cargo word is dropped

parts.note: a load is a cargo
RTA is the British abbreviation for a road traffic accident

explanation.surface: A crash blocks a lorry's cargo from coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the cargo word to LOA, and 'return of' turns it to AOL. RTA is a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood, so this adjective means relating to that vessel.

clue.text: Group primarily isolated and pure in retreat

definitions.text: Group primarily isolated and pure in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the assembled letters read right to left

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word isolated is used

parts.note: mere in the old sense means pure or unmixed

explanation.surface: A community of the solitary and chaste, living withdrawn from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: SET + I + MERE, read backwards. The whole clue also describes these hermits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermits are religious recluses who live apart, chaste and secluded.

clue.text: Planetary ring in huge overlapping series

indicators.note: overlapping means the two words share a letter where they meet, so one copy goes

parts.note: an epic effort is a huge one
a cycle is a series, as of songs or stories

explanation.surface: A planetary ring caught up in a vast run of overlapping events.
explanation.walkthrough: EPIC and CYCLE overlap on their shared C, giving EPICYCLE. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In old astronomy a planet moved on a small circle whose centre travelled round a larger orbit.

clue.text: Prosperous residential area of Bruxelles on the up

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the letters read upwards
of says the letters come from inside the next word

explanation.surface: A well-off suburb of the Belgian capital that is improving.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five letters of BRUXELLES, read upwards, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-to-do district beyond the suburbs of a city is so called.

clue.text: Sib accepts Spaniard's cry of approval for his jacket

indicators.note: accepts means the brother word takes the cheer inside it

parts.note: a sibling, here a brother, is bro
ole is the Spanish shout of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A brother takes a cheer from a Spaniard for his jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' is just a link to the definition: the jacket belongs to the brother in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A short open jacket of Spanish style is a bolero.

clue.text: Does repeatedly run over, i.e. restate, excitedly

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters get agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes over the same ground, saying things again in an excited way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges IE and RESTATE into EITERATES. 'over' is a link word, and 'Does' is the verb, not a female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat oneself is to say or do something again and again.

clue.text: The old record's little dog's cry

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: An old record of a small dog barking.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp high bark, as from a small dog, is called this.

clue.text: Pipe loud instrument

parts.note: F is forte, the music abbreviation for loud
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A pipe described as a noisy musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, and this is one played sideways.

clue.text: Paper hat for a clown

definitions.meaning: a large size of writing paper

explanation.definitionFit: Both a size of writing sheet named after its watermark and the cap a jester wore.

clue.text: Post packet once boat has left

indicators.note: has left means the vessel word is removed

parts.note: a packet was formerly a mail boat carrying post
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parcel posted once the ship has sailed.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet (or packet boat) was a ship carrying mail; take BOAT out of MAILBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Post and mail are synonyms for letters and parcels sent.

clue.text: Leaders of men having ruled Jaipur, each supported by a prince

annotationWithheld.why: Leaders of men having ruled Jaipur, each supported by a prince (8): initials M H R J each followed by an A ('each supported by a'); the grammar has no one-op way to set A under each of four picks, and splitting needs 'Leaders of' on four ops
annotationWithheld.clue: Leaders of men having ruled Jaipur, each supported by a prince

clue.text: Eccentric party in Sunderland?

definitions.meaning: Sunderland stands on the River Wear, so a do there might be a Wear do

explanation.walkthrough: Sunderland is a city in north-east England on the River Wear; a party is a do.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is an oddball; the second reading puns on the river through the city.

clue.text: Pro tem makes numberless calls

indicators.note: numberless means the abbreviation for number is taken away

parts.note: to ring up is to telephone or call

explanation.surface: A temporary professional makes phone calls without numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for number. 'Pro tem' means for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig something up is to assemble it as a makeshift for now.

clue.text: Intermittently, a Czech packing a gun confronts base, very Russian invader

indicators.note: packing means the gun word holds the selected letters inside it

parts.note: the Bren is a light machine gun

indicators.note: Intermittently picks every third letter of a Czech, giving the Z and the H

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A Czech with a gun faces down a Russian invading army.
explanation.walkthrough: Every third letter of 'a Czech' gives Z and H. 'confronts' is a link word. Brezhnev led the 1968 Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet leader sent tanks to crush the Prague Spring in 1968.

clue.text: Make money from Bond?

parts.note: a bond is a certificate you can turn into cash, not the spy; the question mark flags the play

explanation.definitionFit: To convert a bond or cheque into money is to cash it in.

clue.text: Critical interpretation of Exodus, for example, first book lacking info

parts.note: Ex is the standard abbreviation for the book of Exodus

indicators.note: lacking means the information word is taken out

parts.note: Genesis is the first book of the Bible
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A scholarly reading of Exodus and other books, missing information.
explanation.walkthrough: GENESIS loses GEN, leaving ESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is the close critical explanation of a text, especially scripture.

clue.text: Photograph by Man, say

parts.note: x means by, as in measurements such as 3 x 4
Man Ray was a surrealist photographer, so Man suggests Ray

explanation.surface: A picture taken by the photographer Man Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph is a photograph made with penetrating rays.

clue.text: First of all seductive, afterwards grotesque, Angelina in Beowulf, for example

indicators.note: First of all means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Angelina Jolie, seductive and then grotesque, in the film Beowulf.
explanation.walkthrough: Angelina Jolie played Grendel's mother in the 2007 film Beowulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is an Old English heroic poem, a classic epic tale.

clue.text: French physicist takes in key papal courts

indicators.note: takes in means the physicist's name holds the key letter

parts.note: Pierre Curie was a French physicist
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: A French scientist gets into the Vatican's courts.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside CURIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal administration; its Latin plural names its courts and departments.

clue.text: Fuel wild gossip

parts.note: wild things are natural, untamed
gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Wild gossip fuelling the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like an anagram signal but GOSSIP has too few letters; it is a synonym here.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane piped from underground is a common fuel for heating and cooking.

clue.text: Scoff endless cumin

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: jeera is the Hindi name for cumin used in Indian cooking

explanation.surface: Wolf down a spice with no end to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like eat greedily; here it means mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock, and to mock someone loudly is to taunt.
